summary: Phase 149O.20J.6 -- Class-B macOS ACL-Only Higher-Ancestor Detection Repair Independent Verification: independently re-derived HBDC-REQ-016/017/020 directly from docs/contracts/HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md, the real macOS ACL grammar from `man chmod`'s ACL MANIPULATION OPTIONS section and fresh chmod +a grants, and the mode-marker unreliability from a fresh com.apple.provenance xattr probe -- trusting none of 149O.20J.5's report, tests, rights vocabulary, or ACL description. Independently confirmed 0b2fd134 as the true immediate parent of repair commit 6a265e09 via git rev-parse 6a265e09^, extracted the exact pre-repair _acl_grants_agent_write_macos verbatim via git show (not retyped), and reproduced the historical marker-gate + substring-search defect against a fresh real chmod +a add_file,delete_child fixture at POSIX mode 500 with PATH restricted to /usr/bin:/bin (avoiding this dev host's user-writable PATH entries): the historical function misclassified a ground-truth-verified ACL-writable directory as non-write. Independently re-derived the real ACL grammar: numbered entry-line form, user:/group: principal spelling, and confirmed write(file)/add_file(dir) and append(file)/add_subdirectory(dir) render the identical underlying NFSv4 ACE contextually via a direct cross-grant experiment (not assumed from prose). Confirmed the com.apple.provenance xattr is present and non-removable on this host, explaining the +-vs-@ marker substitution, while independently stating the security-relevant conclusion (the marker is not a reliable ACL-presence signal) separately from the host-specific explanation, and confirmed via source inspection that the current parser contains no '+' marker literal anywhere. Wrote a fresh, independent 67-test module (tests/test_phase_149o_20j_6_class_b_acl_only_higher_ancestor_detection_repair_independent_verification.py; zero tests copied from 149O.20J.5's suite; fresh fixtures throughout) covering directory/file rights (each ground-truth-verified via a capability-specific real probe), the man-chmod rights vocabulary, principal resolution (current/unrelated user, effective/unrelated group using real, non-special-cased gid 12 and gid 27, unresolvable/malformed principals), allow/deny direction, malformed/unknown-right fail-closed behavior (parametrized over 8 malformed shapes plus 3 unknown-right combinations), one- and two-level real ancestor-chain composition (using the same host-boundary-stubbing technique 149O.20J.5's own suite independently arrived at, for the identical reason: this dev host's own home directory is agent-writable, an unavoidable confound for any tmp_path-rooted real-filesystem-root walk), Trusted-Git and Protected-Root composition and equivalence, the full B-149O.20J.2-1/J-1/J-2/symlink/indeterminate-ACL regression set, HMIC non-binding (25/5, independently re-extracted), zero-production-consumer confirmation (git grep across src/), the read-only wall (source-inspected for mutating calls), and real-host NON_COMPLIANT. All 67 tests pass, deterministic across repeated runs, zero repository mutation (git status --porcelain -- src/ identical before/after). Independently re-derived two host-specific ACL nuances not previously documented: (1) open(file, 'a') is an O_APPEND open, checked by macOS against the separate `append` right, not `write` -- a write-only grant does not authorize an O_APPEND open even though a plain O_WRONLY open (confirmed via dd) succeeds; (2) an explicit ACL deny entry on a right blocks even the object's owner from exercising that right, overriding ordinary owner-mode-bit authority for that one right, which required explicit ACL-stripping fixture teardown to avoid leaving unremovable pytest tmp directories. CENTRAL FINDING: `man chmod`, read directly on this host, defines writesecurity as "Write an object's security information (ownership, mode, ACL)" and chown as "Change an object's ownership" -- both self-evidently transitive write-equivalent authority (a writesecurity holder can grant itself add_file/write/etc. via ACL edit or flip mode bits directly; a chown holder can become owner and gain mode-bit write), yet both remain classified in _MACOS_ACL_KNOWN_SAFE_RIGHTS by the current (149O.20J.5) production implementation. 149O.20J.5's own doc justifies this as 'empirically confirmed to not confer any effective write authority when granted alone' -- independently reproduced the exact test conditions that claim rests on and confirmed it is a same-owner test: on a single-user host the tester is always the object's owner, and an owner can already chmod their own mode-500 un-ACL'd object with NO ACL grant at all (independently demonstrated), so granting vs. not granting writesecurity/chown is not a meaningful differential test in a same-owner fixture -- it cannot distinguish the ACE's own effect from pre-existing owner authority, and the only principal HBDC-REQ-009 actually contemplates holding such a grant (a non-owner agent against an admin-owned ancestor) was never tested. No second real user account was available on this host for a genuine cross-principal test; the finding rests on man chmod's own unambiguous primary-source definition, the same authoritative documentation this entire repair's rights vocabulary is derived from. Per the governing prompt's explicit criterion ('If the latter [false negative safe] is possible, the repair is not complete'), this is exactly that case. Independently re-confirmed (matching 149O.20J.5's own claims, arrived at independently rather than copied): J-3 historical scope adjudication (original B-CBV-J-3 finding named ancestor-ACL blindness; 149O.20J.2's own verification of that claim used only simulated/forced ACL results, confirmed via direct inspection of that phase's own document text); the two removed 149O.20J.4 xfail markers were pre-authorized by their own reason text and are now genuinely passing; production diff for 6a265e09 confirmed limited to exactly hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py; HMIC frozen scope unchanged (25/5); zero production consumers outside the three-module island; read-only wall intact; real-host NON_COMPLIANT. B-149O.20J.4-1: REPAIRED (marker/grammar defect, independently verified) -- A DISTINCT KNOWN-SAFE-VOCABULARY GAP FOUND (writesecurity/chown) -- NOT CLOSED. CBV-S1: OPEN -- HMIC SOURCE-SCOPE BINDING STILL PENDING. CBV-S10: OPEN -- READINESS CONTRACT/INTEGRATION GAP, unchanged. Class-B: CONTRACT VERIFIED -- MARKER/GRAMMAR DEFECT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- KNOWN-SAFE-VOCABULARY GAP OPEN -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable.
